title: Dedicated autoscaling: add per-account/deployment feature flags for predictive mode + safe rollback path
author: Diego Santos
description:
Context: Predictive autoscaling is entering pilot and we need a hard on/off switch that can be applied at the account and (optionally) deployment level, with deterministic behavior and a safe rollback path. Today, predictive mode is effectively enabled via config wiring and is hard to quickly disable without pushing config changes or code changes.

What this PR changes: 1) Adds a dedicated feature flag gate for predictive autoscaling that can be evaluated per account_id and optionally narrowed to deployment_id. 2) Implements a safe rollback path in the autoscaler loop: if the flag is off (or evaluation fails/stales), predictive inputs are ignored and we fall back to reactive desired capacity computation, while still enforcing min/max bounds. 3) Adds rollout tooling for internal operators: a small admin endpoint + CLI subcommand to set/clear the flag for an account or (account, deployment) pair with audit log emission. 4) Adds metrics for visibility into flag evaluation and fallback reasons.

Semantics / precedence: - Effective predictive_enabled = feature_flag(account_id, deployment_id) AND scaling_policy.predictive_mode == ON. - If predictive_mode == OFF, we never call the predictor regardless of flags. - If predictive_mode == ON but feature flag is OFF, we skip prediction and behave as reactive autoscaling. - If feature flag evaluation errors or is stale, we treat it as OFF (fail-closed) and emit a counter + structured log entry. - Bounds are enforced after desired capacity is computed (reactive or predictive) per ADR precedence.

Safety: - Fail-closed on flag lookup failure or cache staleness. - Explicit rollback behavior is exercised in tests: turning the flag off mid-ramp forces the autoscaler to ignore forecast input on the next tick (no sticky predictive state). - Rate limits on admin updates are not included here (handled in follow-up); this PR does, however, debounce cache refresh to avoid hot looping.

Operational notes: - Flag evaluation is cached for 30s with jitter to avoid a thundering herd from all autoscaler loops across the fleet. - Audit events: CAPACITY_FLAG_UPDATED includes actor, account_id, optional deployment_id, old_value/new_value, and request_id.

Testing: - Unit tests for evaluator precedence and fail-closed behavior. - Integration test with a fake predictor: verifies that disabling the flag stops forecast calls and reverts to reactive decisions on the next tick. - Load test (local sim) to validate cache behavior under N deployments.

Rollout plan: - Default OFF for all accounts. - Pilot enablement via internal helpdesk (INT-9412) or on-call runbook steps; start with 1 account + 1 deployment in us-east, then expand by account.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added - [x] Metrics + logs added - [x] Docs/runbook references added (internal) - [x] Backward compatible (no behavior change unless enabled)
commits: control-plane/flags: introduce PredictiveAutoscalingFlag with account+deployment targeting
autoscaler: gate predictor calls behind flag + policy toggle; add fallback reasons
admin: add internal endpoint + CLI to set/clear predictive autoscaling flag
observability: emit flag_eval_result + fallback counters; add structured logs
tests: coverage for precedence, fail-closed, and rollback on next tick
conversation: Ethan Park (review): Can we clarify precedence between scaling_policy.predictive_mode and the feature flag? I want deterministic semantics in the autoscaler regardless of cache state.

Diego Santos (author): Updated description + code comment: effective predictive_enabled = policy.predictive_mode == ON && flag == true. Cache miss/error now fails closed (treated as OFF) and we log + metric fallback_reason=flag_eval_failed.
Vanessa Ortiz (review): Concern about caching TTL (30s) delaying rollback during an incident. Can we ensure turning OFF is observed quickly?

Diego Santos (author): Added jittered TTL but also a fast-path invalidation in the admin update handler (publishes an invalidate message). Autoscaler cache subscribes; in practice rollback is next tick (<10s) after invalidate, worst-case 30s if subscriber is down (still safe, but slower). Added integration test to validate next-tick rollback when invalidate is received.

Rafael Mendes (SRE): Please add a metric that shows how many deployments are gated OFF by flag while policy is ON (helps confirm pilot enablement) and explicitly fail-closed on feature flag service errors.

Diego Santos (author): Added counter redwood.dedicated.autoscaling.predictive.gated_off_total{reason=flag_off|flag_eval_failed|policy_off}. Feature flag fetch errors increment flag_eval_failed and treat as OFF.
Miles Thornton (reliability): Any risk of high-cardinality labels? Please do not label metrics with account_id/deployment_id.
Diego Santos (author): Agreed. Metrics only include reason + region + env. Account/deployment identifiers remain in structured logs/audit events only.
Lauren Bishop (PM): This unblocks pilot enablement. Can we confirm default behavior remains unchanged for existing Dedicated customers?
Diego Santos (author): Yes: default OFF for all; policy toggle remains OFF unless explicitly set. No behavior change unless both are enabled.
Rafael Mendes: Approved (with note to link runbook in pilot doc)
Diego Santos (author): Added link in internal runbook section and updated INT-9412 template.
release_notes: Internal: Added per-account/per-deployment feature flag gating for predictive autoscaling with fail-closed behavior and a safe rollback path. Pilot enablement via admin endpoint/CLI; emits audit events and metrics for gating/fallback reasons.
